simultaneously: the kernels' input schema, the decision record's schema,
and the backtest's input schema. One artefact, three consumers. That is
what makes spec s5.17's equivalence requirement a type rather than a
promise, and it is why this is a `contract=` file (doc 03 s5.1) rather
Changing it is a major version. CI fails if the enrichment modules produce

state_encoding.$comment: Observed[T] is two columns, value and state. Four states, and NOT_APPLICABLE is not a data-quality state — it means the field is structurally absent for this event type. Collapsing it into ABSENT makes an aggregate outage and a login indistinguishable.

columns.name: amount_zar_cents
columns.$comment: int64 cents. Never float, never Decimal (doc 03 s1.2, doc 05 s1.5).

columns.name: client_segment_bits
columns.$comment: 46 of 64 bits used. Segment definition version resolved at event_timestamp.

columns.name: mule_list_membership
columns.$comment: The interval id, not a boolean. The dispute pack needs 'added 09:11 on 2 March by the consortium feed', which a boolean cannot carry.

columns.name: client_count_1min
columns.$comment: One of 168. Watermark recorded, state derived from it before the kernel — the kernel sees the state, not the watermark, because a rule reasons about staleness and never about clocks.

columns.name: card_model_score
columns.$comment: Absence carries a reason: timeout / error / circuit_open / not_requested. A replay reads the recorded absence, never re-requests.

availability.$comment: Per-column, per-event-type, effective-dated. This is the check that makes 'a rule referencing a field its event type does not carry' a build error rather than a 02:00 page, and it is what lets a backtest over 18 months be honest about a field that did not exist before 2026-04-01 (spec s11.6).
